proposals.warning: At the **22 October 2026** nine-month trading update, trigger a full re-read if RELX withdraws its full-year expectation of strong underlying revenue, adjusted operating profit and adjusted EPS growth, or ceases to describe cost growth as running below revenue growth. That would be the first dated evidence that operating leverage is fading while buybacks still lift per-share figures; it is a warning, not an automatic sale ([current outlook](https://www.relx.com/media/press-releases/year-2026/first-half-2026), [financial calendar](https://www.relx.com/investors/financial-calendar)).
proposals.break: At the FY2026 results, to be checked by **15 February 2027**, put the position under §5.1 if adjusted cash-flow conversion falls below **95%** and net debt/EBITDA rises above **2.5×** after the announced £2.25bn buyback. Both conditions together would show that per-share growth is being supported by a weaker cash engine and higher leverage rather than improving business economics; the H1 reference points are 98% and 2.3× ([half-year results](https://www.relx.com/media/press-releases/year-2026/first-half-2026)).

proposals.warning: At the FY2026 result currently estimated for 5 November 2026, trigger a full re-read if net sales are below management's $1.470bn lower bound, adjusted EBITDA is below $367m, or free cash flow is no more than 70% of adjusted net income. Any miss is the first hard evidence that pricing and execution are not carrying into the full year; it is a warning, not an automatic sale ([company outlook](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350593/000135059326000034/exhibit991pressreleasefy26.htm), [local result date](../../prices.json)).
proposals.break: At the Q2 FY2027 filing, to be checked no later than 7 May 2027, put the position under §5.1 if trailing-twelve-month GAAP operating margin is below 17.0% while trailing-twelve-month revenue growth is below 3.0%. That combination would show that tariff refunds, compensation timing and pricing produced a peak rather than a durable reset in a growing business; it directly tests the dominant risk ([current filing and baseline](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1350593/000135059326000036/mwa-20260630.htm)).

proposals.warning: At the Q3 2026 filing scheduled for **29 October 2026**, trigger a full re-read if transaction-fee revenue growth trails total ADV growth by **15 percentage points or more** while total variable fees per million also decline by **more than 10% year on year**. Q2 showed the milder version—18.2% ADV growth, 8.3% transaction-fee growth and a 7.2% fee decline—so this is the first dated test of worsening monetisation rather than an automatic sale ([Q2 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1758730/000175873026000133/tw-20260630.htm), [local result date](../../prices.json)).
proposals.break: At the FY2026 10-K, to be checked by **1 March 2027**, put the position under §5.1 if two consecutive quarters have both (a) flat or declining transaction-fee revenue despite positive ADV growth and (b) year-on-year declines in Tradeweb's fully electronic U.S. high-grade and high-yield TRACE shares. That combination would show that neither monetisation nor electronic market share is compounding, directly breaking the business case; Q2 reference shares were 19.0% in high grade and 8.5% in high yield, both up year on year ([Q2 company release](https://investors.tradeweb.com/static-files/e5696c92-ff61-4d32-85b0-678deedf8d9a)).
